description: Following the public release of Kimi K3 and the demonstrated offensive cyber capabilities now in circulation, a coalition of European biosecurity researchers and public health agencies issues a joint warning about the potential for AI-designed pathogens to bypass current screening protocols. The report does not describe a specific attack but argues that the combination of open-weight models and accessible wet-lab automation has lowered the barrier to entry enough to require urgent policy attention. This creates political momentum for new biological design controls even before a major incident occurs.
